Each disclaims validated effectiveness, but the phrase names an operational-validity activity no recorded study performs (studies are closed), and the sources treat operational validity as an unmeasured property. Exceeds the source-aligned evidence; not reopened as a wording repair here.

JRS is in operational validation and makes no claim of validated effectiveness.

items.category: Numerical rating on the training page
items.finding: The training page has reviewers assign a one-to-five "Decision Defensibility Score". The October 3 sources do not address human training ratings; the handoff limits numerical DRR scoring by the Engine and evaluation tooling. Whether a human training rating is consistent with that limit is an owner decision.

The Manifest page describes a public specification, no public Manifest output, and an unsigned hash that does not prove authorship. The October 3 sources observed (2 October, production) pages describing authenticated development Manifest output; this branch narrowed that under the handoff.
present: An unsigned Manifest can be checked for internal consistency, but it does not prove who created it.

items.finding: The Standard page lists review environments including HR and employment documentation. The sources limit use of the diagnostic to non-HR records; whether that limit governs the public methodology, or only the Engine and evaluation, is not stated.
present: HR review and employment documentation audit

items.finding: On this branch the security and privacy pages no longer state the 90-day field-level expiry that the repository retention policy sets (introduced by 3758d76; guard check "disclosed retention matches the policy"). The sources record that published policy is not evidence of execution; the disclosure itself is a counsel matter (RG-3).
Calibration, audit and engagement pages and the terms page are marked closed or retained only for engagements agreed before 4 September 2026.
